uncited: *   **Inputs:** Canonical 3D Gaussian attributes (position $\mu_c$, rotation $r_c$, scale $s$, color, opacity), joint transformation matrices $M_{j,t}$ derived from a parametric body model (e.g., SMPL) for each training timestep $t$, and initial learnable skinning weights $w$.
*   **Skinned Weights ($w$):** A vector of size $J$ (total number of joints) per Gaussian.
*   **Joint Transformation Matrices ($M_{j,t}$):** Precomputed rigid transformation matrices for each joint $j$ and timestep $t$.
**Optimize Skinning Weights:** Initialize learnable per-Gaussian skinning weights vector $w$.
**Activate and Normalize Weights:** Apply ReLU activation to each component $w_j$ of the skinning weights vector to ensure non-negativity.
*   **Negative Weights:** During optimization, skinning weights $w$ may become negative.
*   **Pose Blend Shapes:** Pose blend shapes are explicitly excluded because shape estimation and obtained blend shapes may be inaccurate.
The specific application of LBS where Gaussians are defined in a canonical space and deformed forward to the observation space.
It differs from inverse skinning by avoiding the need to query the canonical space from observation space points. [Canonical LBS](canonical-lbs.md)
Emphasizes the direction of deformation (canonical to observation).
It is chosen when real-time rendering of posed avatars is required without iterative inverse mapping. [Forward Skinning](forward-skinning.md)
The alternative approach used in NeRF-based methods, mapping observation-space points to canonical space.
It is slower for rendering but can handle complex non-rigid deformations differently. [Inverse Skinning](inverse-skinning.md)
*   **Time Complexity:** $O(N \cdot J)$ per Gaussian per frame, where $N$ is the number of Gaussians and $J$ is the number of joints.
The precomputation of joint transforms is $O(J)$.
*   **Memory Complexity:** $O(N \cdot J)$ to store skinning weights.
Joint transforms are $O(J)$ per timestep.
*   **Measured Performance:** Not given in the sources.
*   **Strengths:** Avoids inaccuracies from pose blend shapes; efficient precomputation of joint transforms; direct transformation of Gaussian attributes.

*   **Limitations:** Relies on the accuracy of the parametric body model (e.g., SMPL); skinning weights are static after training, limiting per-frame adaptability; negative weights must be handled via ReLU and normalization.
*   **When to use:** Real-time rendering of animatable avatars where pose-dependent deformations are handled by an MLP and rigid joint transformations are sufficient for the base deformation.

*   **When not to use:** When high-fidelity non-rigid deformations beyond rigid joint transformations are required without additional MLP capacity, or when inverse mapping is preferred for specific rendering pipelines.
Linear Blend Skinning for Gaussian Splatting was introduced in the context of human avatar modeling using 3D Gaussian Splatting.
It builds on the SMPL body model and adapts LBS to work with canonical Gaussians.
